detail: Random-effects meta-analysis (blocker.stan): one row per trial (22 trials), treatment (nt,rt) and control (nc,rc) arms in the same row (wide); the study-level random effect delta[N] is observation-level (one row per study), no grouping column in the table.

Latent-trait/item-response model (bones.stan): the loaded table holds item parameters (ncat, delta, gamma_1..4) for 34 indicators, not observations; the response (grade, child-by-indicator matrix) and the grouping (child, theta[nChild]) are not columns.
Avoidance-learning model (dogs.stan): wide table, 30 dogs as rows and 25 trials as Y_1..Y_25 columns; only fixed effects (alpha, beta), no random effect; grouping unit (dog) is no long column.

One-way variance-components model (dyes.stan): wide table, 6 batches as rows and 5 samples as y_1..y_5 columns; the batch random effect is a row and samples are columns, so the grouping factor is no column of the loaded table.

Hierarchical Poisson (epil.stan): wide table, 59 patients as rows and 4 visits as y_1..y_4 columns; per-patient random effects index rows (observation-level) and visit is columns; grouping unit is no long column.
Bioequivalence cross-over (equiv.stan): wide table, 10 subjects as rows and 2 periods as Y_1,Y_2 columns; the subject random effect delta[N] indexes rows (observation-level) and period is columns.

Weibull frailty survival (kidney.stan). RULE GAP: the loader tabulated only the length-18 right-censored arrays (age_rc, sex_rc, patient_rc, t_rc, disease_rc); the 58 uncensored observations and their event times are separate arrays flagged not-in-table, so the loaded table is a censored-only subset (t_rc holds censoring times, patient_rc has 15 of 38 patients, mostly singletons). Excluded as a partial/derived slice; re-file if the full long table is wanted.

Cox regression (leuk.stan): single fixed covariate Z (treatment) and baseline hazard dL0; no random effect and no grouping column (one row per patient). The frailty version leukfr adds the pair random effect and is kept.

Rasch item-response model (lsat.stan): wide/aggregated table of 32 response patterns (response_1..5 items as columns, culm = cumulative pattern counts); the student random effect theta[N] indexes 1000 students not in the table.

Random-effects meta-analysis (magnesium.stan): one row per study (8 studies), treatment (nt,rt) and control (nc,rc) arms in the same row (wide); the study-level random effect theta is observation-level, no grouping column.

Weibull regression (mice.stan): beta[group] is a fixed effect per dose group (M=4, flat normal(0,100) prior, no hyperparameter), not a random effect; only 4 groups; loaded table is the uncensored subset (group_uncensored, t_uncensored). Fixed-effects fit, no hierarchical model.

Case-control smoothing of log-odds (oxford.stan): wide table, one row per year-stratum (120 strata), case arm (r1,n1) and control arm (r0,n0) in the same row; the per-stratum random effect b[K] is observation-level.
Gamma-Poisson failure model (pump.stan): 10 pumps as 10 rows (count x, exposure t); theta[N] is a per-pump gamma random effect, observation-level (one Poisson row per pump), no grouping column.
Poisson GLMM with overdispersion (salm.stan): wide table, 6 doses as rows and 3 plates as y_1..y_3 columns; the dose random effect lambda indexes rows (observation-level) and plates are columns.
Same as salm (salm2.stan, uncentred covariates): wide table of 6 doses x 3 plates (y_1..y_3); the dose random effect is observation-level and plates are columns.
Binomial GLMM with overdispersion (seeds.stan): 21 plates as 21 rows (n of N, covariates x1, x2); the plate random effect b[I] is observation-level (one binomial row per plate), no grouping column.
Robust/ridge linear regression (stacks_a_normal.stan, normal error): 21 rows (response Y, predictors x_1..x_3); only fixed effects beta and a residual scale, no random effect or grouping column.

Robust/ridge linear regression (stacks_b_dexp.stan, double-exponential error): 21 rows (response Y, predictors x_1..x_3); only fixed effects beta and a residual scale, no random effect or grouping column.
Robust/ridge linear regression (stacks_c_t4.stan, Student-t error): 21 rows (response Y, predictors x_1..x_3); only fixed effects beta and a residual scale, no random effect or grouping column.

Robust/ridge linear regression (stacks_d_normal_ridge.stan, normal-error ridge): 21 rows (response Y, predictors x_1..x_3); only fixed effects beta and a residual scale, no random effect or grouping column.

Robust/ridge linear regression (stacks_e_dexp_ridge.stan, double-exponential ridge): 21 rows (response Y, predictors x_1..x_3); only fixed effects beta and a residual scale, no random effect or grouping column.
Robust/ridge linear regression (stacks_f_t4_ridge.stan, Student-t ridge): 21 rows (response Y, predictors x_1..x_3); only fixed effects beta and a residual scale, no random effect or grouping column.

Binomial random-effects model (surgical.stan): 12 hospitals as 12 rows (r deaths of n operations); the hospital random intercept b[N] is observation-level (one binomial row per hospital), no grouping column.
Binomial dose-response GLM (beetles_cloglog.stan, cloglog link): 8 dose groups as rows (r of n at dose x); only fixed effects alpha, beta, no random effect or grouping column.
Binomial dose-response GLM (beetles_logit.stan, logit link): 8 dose groups as rows (r of n at dose x); only fixed effects alpha, beta, no random effect or grouping column.
Binomial dose-response GLM (beetles_probit.stan, probit link): 8 dose groups as rows (r of n at dose x); only fixed effects alpha, beta, no random effect or grouping column.

Case-control logistic regression with covariate measurement error (cervix2.stan): loaded table is the 115 complete-case records (wc, dc, xc); only fixed effects (beta0C, beta, phi, q), no random effect or grouping column.
Same model and data as cervix (cervix2.stan); 115 complete-case records (wc, dc, xc), fixed effects only, no random effect or grouping column.
Zero-inflated/mixture count model (hearts.stan): 12 patients as 12 rows (x, y, t); only fixed effects alpha, delta, no random effect or grouping column.

Age-cohort Poisson smoothing (ice.stan): the year effect beta has a second-order random-walk (smoothing) prior over an ordered time axis, not an exchangeable zero-mean grouping random effect; age is a fixed effect. No grouping factor in the GLMM sense (time-series smoothing).
Same data and model as ice (ice.stan); age-cohort Poisson with a random-walk smoothing prior over year and fixed age; no exchangeable grouping factor.
Same data and model as ice (ice.stan); age-cohort Poisson with a random-walk smoothing prior over year and fixed age; no exchangeable grouping factor.

Repeated-measures multivariate-normal ANOVA (jaws.stan): the loaded table holds the age vector (4 ages) and the 4x4 prior/scatter covariance matrix (S_1..S_4), not observations; the jaw-measurement matrix Y (subjects x ages) and the subject grouping are not columns.

Hierarchical nonlinear (logistic) growth, MVN version (mvn_orange.stan): the loaded table holds only prior hyperparameters (mu_var_prior, invR covariance matrices, mu_m_prior); the growth observations Y (5 trees x 7 times) and time x are not columns, and the tree grouping is not in the table.

Hierarchical nonlinear (logistic) growth (orange.stan): wide table, 5 trees as rows and 7 measurement times as Y_1..Y_7 columns; the tree random coefficients theta[K] index rows and times are columns, so the grouping factor is no long column.
Bayesian model choice between two non-nested linear regressions (pines.stan): 42 rows (y, x, z); no random effect and no grouping column.
Data-cloning variant of the vol1 seeds binomial GLMM (seeds.stan): 21 plates as 21 rows; the plate random effect is observation-level (one binomial row per plate), no grouping column.
